'''Gkuthaarn''',  also rendered '''Kuthant''',  '''Kutanda''' and other variant spellings, is an extinct [[Paman languages|Paman language]] of the [[Cape York Peninsula]], [[Queensland]], [[Australia]]. It also known as '''Karundi'''/'''Garandi''' (and variant spellings), but the [[Garandi language]] may be a separate dialect.

[[Norman Tindale]] also assigned the name [[Kareldi]], but this is not confirmed by others.<ref name=G31>{{AIATSIS|G31|Ghutkaarn}}</ref> Current sources refer to the [[Gkuthaarn]] people.<ref>{{cite web | title=Gkuthaarn Kukatj Indigenous Land & Sea Ranger | website=Carpentaria Land Council Aboriginal Corporation | date=September 2020 | url=http://www.clcac.com.au/news/corporate-news/2020/169 | access-date=13 October 2020 | archive-date=14 October 2020 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201014072803/http://www.clcac.com.au/news/corporate-news/2020/169 | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last=Barry | first=Derek | title=Native title win for Gkuthaarn and Kukatj people | website=The North West Star | date=30 September 2020 | url=https://www.northweststar.com.au/story/6948210/native-title-win-for-gkuthaarn-and-kukatj-people/ | access-date=13 October 2020}}</ref>

==Alternative names==
;Tindale:
*Kotanda, also spelt Kutanda, Goothanto<ref name=G31/>
*Karundi, also spelt Karunti, Kurandi, Ka-rantee, Karrandi, Karrandee, Gar-und-yih, thought to be derived from Karun-/Gooran, meaning [[scrublands]] people.<ref name=G31/>

However, according to [[Lauriston Sharp]], Kotanda was also used for the now extinct [[Kalibamu]], and [[Garandi language|Karandi/Garandi]] ([[AUSTLANG]] G32) was a different local group,<ref name=G31/> and [[AIATSIS]] agrees.<ref name=G32>{{AIATSIS|G32|Garandi}}</ref>

;Other variants
Other variant spellings included in AUSTLANG are:<ref name=G31/>
*Karaldi
*Gudanda
*Gudhanda
*Gudhand
*Guandhar
